correctness.rationale: For any graph on at least seven vertices without triangles or four-cycles, the Alexander dual X of the ordinary three-cut complex consists of the complete graph plus precisely its connected induced 3-vertex paths as 2-simplices: all triples in any 4-set cannot be connected without creating a four-cycle. Each triangle has a unique nonedge between path endpoints, present in no other triangle by absence of four-cycles, giving literal free-face collapses to a connected graph of cycle rank \(b=\binom{n-1}{2}-\sum_v\binom{\deg(v)}{2}\). Integral Alexander duality leaves exactly top homology \(H_{n-4}\cong\mathbb Z^b\) in the original complex. Its complete codimension-one skeleton, in dimension at least three, lets Hurewicz and Whitehead then produce the wedge homotopy equivalence even in the contractible case. The injection of oriented path triangles into the exterior square of the rational augmentation representation and equivariant Alexander duality with the sign of the ambient vertex permutation prove the full automorphism character. All hypotheses and signs independently checked in directly enumerated finite examples; 374 automorphism actions and full mod-2 ranks for six graphs were verified by executing the bundled standalone verifier. These experiments check the proof but are not its replacement.

originality.rationale: Distinct new components are the global elimination of the potential lower-degree homology in ordinary three-cut complexes for all triangle- and square-free simple graphs (including disconnected graphs), the resulting exact integral homotopy type, and the complete rational graph-automorphism character via a signed path-chain injection. Bayer et al. 2304.13675 Theorem 6.1 and Proposition 6.2 already supply full lower skeleton, a torsion-free two-degree range, and Euler count; these are explicitly credited and not claimed as new. Published cycle, tree and hexagonal-grid results and isolated specific-graph computations cover special cases but do not imply the all-graph equivariant character. A prior related diameter<=2 result gives a \(\Delta_2\) to \(\Delta_3\) collapse on a strictly narrower class; it does not apply to \(C_7\) (diameter 3, three-cut Betti 8 while graph cycle rank 1). None of the inspected full primary-text sections or relevant semantic results contained an equivalent general formula. This remains a same-model originality assessment with explicit residual literature risk, not a statement of global uniqueness.
residual_risks: Alternative published equivalence through graph hyperedge boundaries, Alexander dual collapse, or poset topology could subsume the proof without using ordinary three-cut terminology; search does not rule this out.
Special graph families and Betti values are previously covered; the new assertion is the unrestricted short-cycle-free theorem and automorphism character, not those special numbers.
Finite tests are only corroboration. Independent audit and unrestricted external literature validation have not been performed.

value.rationale: A complete natural class of all finite graphs with no 3- or 4-cycles (including disconnected, high-degree, cyclic, and highly symmetric graphs) receives one integral homotopy-type classification and an explicit full Aut(G) character. This is not merely the Euler number: the original theorem left open the possibility of lower-degree homology, and numerical Betti values do not identify representation modules. The private-endpoint-edge collapse and signed-path exact sequence are structural tools reusable for classifying more graph complexes; the at least seven vertices boundary has a topological reason (Hurewicz after full lower skeleton). For example, \(C_7\) has 8 three-cut top spheres whereas its 2-cut cycle rank is 1; Petersen and Heawood examples are consistent but not the novelty. No broader classification, shellability theorem, irreducible decomposition or equivariant homotopy type is asserted.
